thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — SLO breach detected for customer Auriga (VPC: auriga-eu-west). p95=640ms, p99=2300ms (threshold p99=1000ms). Error rate steady, but significant tail latency. Incident ID: INC-2099980000. Paging on-call: @elaine.

elaine: ack. I'm oncall. pulling traces and pool metrics now. tagging SRE leads.

raj: i'm awake — seeing GPU saturation on auriga-eu-west dedicated pool. GPUs 94-99% across replicas, queue length spiking. KV cache hit down to ~33%. suspect cache churn after a large tenant deployment this morning.

jess: on logs — I see a spike of many long context requests from tenant auriga-app-42 starting ~2099979800. They pushed a new model variant that increases seq lengths.

elaine: customer traffic looks normal in qps but average seq_len doubled for a subset. that explains CPU/GPU time per request.

raj: quick mitigation options: 1) scale pool by +2 replicas (fast), 2) apply tenant isolation (move auriga-app-42 to reserved lane), 3) route a portion of traffic to smaller quantized fallback model in-hosted. prefer do 1+3 asap.

jess: agree. scaling first to reduce queue. then fallback for heavy tails.

elaine: executing scale command now.
```bash
# scale dedicated pool (Auriga eu-west)
rcli pool scale --pool auriga-eu-west --replicas +2 --reason "p99 spike INC-2099980000"
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Starting replica creation — expected ready ~ 180s.

raj: while replicas spin up, let's add a temporary routing rule for auriga to send 30% of traffic to redwood-lite-1-8q (quantized, lower latency). This will target longest requests by header flag.

elaine: creating routing rule.
```bash
rbctl route update --tenant auriga --region eu-west --fallback redwood-lite-1-8q --percent 30 --match "seq_len>2048 || model_variant=heavy"
```

ops-bot: Route update queued. Policy rollout started (gradual 5% every 30s).

mike: @support-runner can you open a customer-facing incident and notify Auriga support contact? include impact: elevated p99, degraded tail latency, mitigation steps (scale + fallback). ETA for next update 15m.

support-runner: opening case now. Case# 123456. Message sent to auriga-ops@auriga.com: "We're investigating elevated p99 latency in eu-west. We've scaled your dedicated pool and partially routed heavy requests to a lower-latency fallback. We're monitoring — will update in 15 minutes." :email:

elaine: replicas are coming online — two new pods reported ready at 2099980125. GPU util dropped to 78% and queue length halved. p99 fell to ~1.4s but still above target.

raj: kv cache miss still high (47%). There may be eviction thrash. Can we temporarily increase KV cache allocation for auriga? that's on the instance config.

jess: we can bump cache size for the dedicated pool but config change needs a short restart of local cache agent (planned <60s). tradeoff: small blip vs sustained lower p99. agree to proceed.

elaine: authorized. Doing cache bump now.
```bash
rcli pool config set --pool auriga-eu-west --kv-cache-size 32GB --apply-restart
```

ops-bot: Rolling restart started for cache agent on pool auriga-eu-west. Expected per-replica restart 12-18s.

raj: restart done on 3/4 replicas, cache_hit now 68% on those; p99 dropped to 980ms at 2099980480. We're under threshold on those replicas, overall p99 now ~1.02s.

elaine: good. overall p99 trending down. continue monitoring for 20m. leave fallback routing at 30% until stable.

mike: assign post-incident: owner @raj, severity Sev2, timeline start=2099980000, mitigation summary: scaled +2, route fallback 30%, bumped KV cache. Need RCA to cover: cause (tenant sequence length change + cache eviction), why autoscale didn't trigger earlier, telemetry gap that hid growing seq_len.

raj: noted. I'll draft RCA and initial timeline.

jess: also add playbook updates: consider proactive detection for sudden seq_len shifts and tenant-level resource reservation flags.

elaine: handing off to morning SRE shift — @jess @raj will own the watch. I'm stepping out at 2099981200. All good to continue.

jess: ack handoff. Monitoring on, will post updates every 15m or on material change.

support-runner: update sent to Auriga: "Latency improved after scaling and cache tuning. We will keep the fallback route active and continue monitoring. Next update in 30 minutes or sooner if anything changes."

mike: thanks team. once stable, please create a concise customer-facing summary for the account team. Also set follow-up call with Auriga if they want deeper review.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2099980000 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: raj. Postmortem assigned.

raj: filing postmortem draft now and adding links to telemetry dashboards + logs. Will include runbook changes and an alert to detect seq_len spikes.

elaine: final note — no request drops observed during mitigation. We avoided fallback to multi-region failover. Good job. :thumbsup:

jess: closing thread for handoff. Will reopen if regression.
